items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Don Redman had them. So they were working out of this Greystone ballroom in Detroit.

ctx.x: Doc Willow? Yeah. Yeah. And Raymond Valentine. And we had Cass Simpson on piano and accordion. And we had Boris Lovingood. He's from, I think Austin, Texas. And we had the, we had the, five brass. And I think we had four reeds. Two pianists and Snagg Jones on the drum. So we had a battle with this, the same McKinney's Cotspickers. Don Redman had them then, you heard of Don Redman had them. So they were working out of this Greystone ballroom in Detroit. So they were booked there. We played the Matinee on Sunday…
Who was this guy, Percy, you were saying? I guess it was back at Bill Bottoms or something.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Later on they played with Don Redmond, Shirley Clay, nice trumpet player.

ctx.x: I talked to him the other day.

He had a studio right there at 36th Estate you know. He had the band in Milwaukee, the Wisconsin roof, before Sims had it. He comes or he leaves there and goes to Savoy. That's when Sims goes on in there and when Sims is about a year or so I go in there with Sims. But he had a good band, he had a good band, he had good Harmon's Bremen. He had Riverview. He and Cook, those fellas, they had some of the best jobs to be had. McGuire's down on Clark Street. I follow Roy and Dutray and him all around. And I get into…
Yeah, he's from Denver but he's been there.
